# Add frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instancesAdd frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instances

An enhanced multi-frame instance describes its frames with functional groups: an optional shared group for what every frame has in common, and one group per frame. Nothing here reads or rewrites them.

Add a `pydicom.multiframe` module, its names also reachable from `pydicom`, holding `frame_attributes(ds, index)`, `varying_attributes(ds)`, `extract_frames(ds, indices)`, `merge_frames(datasets)`, `group_frames(ds, keys)` and `sort_frames(ds, keys)`. `MultiFrameError`, a `ValueError`, is raised for a dataset with no per-frame groups, transfer syntax or pixel data, a shared group sequence present but not holding exactly one item, a frame count absent or disagreeing with those groups, pixel data too short for them, a frame that is not there, an empty selection, a selection naming a frame twice, no keys, a key naming no attribute, values that cannot be compared, and inputs that cannot be combined.

`frame_attributes` returns the attributes held inside the macros that apply to one zero-based frame, the shared macros written first and the frame's own second, a per-frame macro replacing the shared macro carrying its tag. What it returns is a copy, so changing it leaves the instance alone. `varying_attributes` returns the tags whose effective value is not the same for every frame, and nothing for a single frame.

The other four derive a new instance. `extract_frames` keeps the frames named by `indices` in the order given. `merge_frames` takes every frame of every input in turn, and needs them to agree on SOP class, transfer syntax, pixel data element and image pixel attributes. `group_frames` returns one instance per distinct combination of the effective values of `keys`, in order of first appearance, each holding its frames in their old order, frames carrying none of an attribute grouping together. `sort_frames` puts them in ascending order of those values, the first key deciding first, frames missing an attribute after those that have it, ties left as they were. Keys are keywords or tags.

A derived instance always carries one shared group. In-stack position numbers are renumbered from one within each stack, in frame order. A dimension whose frames all carry one index value is then dropped, from the dimension index description and from every frame's index values, an emptied one being removed rather than left empty. What remains is renumbered, each dimension alone, to 1, 2, 3 in the order first seen. Only then is a macro that has the same value for every frame stored once, in the shared group, every other macro being stored in each frame's own group. Whichever pixel data element it carries is rebuilt in the new frame order, encapsulated again if it was, padded to an even length if not, and any extended offset table is dropped. It takes a new SOP instance UID its file meta information agrees with, and a source image sequence with one item per input naming its SOP class, SOP instance UID and the 1-based numbers of frames taken from it. Inputs are left unchanged and share nothing with the result.

Implemented enhanced multi-frame operations in [multiframe.py](/app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py:1), with top-level exports in [__init__.py](/app/src/pydicom/__init__.py:36).

Includes validation, functional-group normalization, extraction/merge/group/sort, pixel rebuilding, UID/source references, and deep-copy isolation.

    """Return the encapsulated pixel data's basic offset table frame offsets.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the
        beginning of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then after reading it will be
        positioned at the start of the item tag of the first fragment after the
        Basic Offset Table.
    endianness : str, optional

        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    -------
    list[int]

        measured from the end of the basic offset table.

    ----------

def generate_frames(
    buffer: bytes | ReadableBuffer,
    *,
    number_of_frames: int | None = None,
    extended_offsets: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | tuple[bytes, bytes] | None = None,
    endianness: str = "<",
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield complete pixel data frames from `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    .. note::

        When the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        isn't supplied then more frames may be yielded than given by
        `number_of_frames` provided there are sufficient excess fragments
        available.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of the basic offset table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then the final offset position depends
        on the number of yielded frames.
    number_of_frames : int, optional
        Required when the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset
        Table has not been supplied. This should be the value of (0028,0008) *Number
        of Frames* or the expected number of frames in the encapsulated data.
    extended_offsets : tuple[list[int], list[int]] or tuple[bytes, bytes], optional
        The (offsets, lengths) of the Extended Offset Table as taken from
        (7FE0,0001) *Extended Offset Table* and (7FE0,0002) *Extended Offset
        Table Lengths* as either the raw encoded values or a list of their
        decoded equivalents.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        The encoded pixel data, one frame at a time.

    References
    ----------
    DICOM Standard Part 5, :dcm:`Annex A <part05/chapter_A.html>`
    """
    fragmented_frames = generate_fragmented_frames(
        buffer,
        number_of_frames=number_of_frames,
        extended_offsets=extended_offsets,
        endianness=endianness,
    )
    for fragments in fragmented_frames:
        yield b"".join(fragments)

def get_expected_length(ds: "Dataset", unit: str = "bytes") -> int:
    """Return the expected length (in terms of bytes or pixels) of the *Pixel
    Data*.

    +------------------------------------------------+-------------+
    | Element                                        | Required or |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+ optional    |
    | Tag         | Keyword                   | Type |             |
    +=============+===========================+======+=============+
    | (0028,0002) | SamplesPerPixel           | 1    | Required    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+
    | (0028,0004) | PhotometricInterpretation | 1    | Required    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+
    | (0028,0008) | NumberOfFrames            | 1C   | Optional    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+
    | (0028,0010) | Rows                      | 1    | Required    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+
    | (0028,0011) | Columns                   | 1    | Required    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+
    | (0028,0100) | BitsAllocated             | 1    | Required    |
    +-------------+---------------------------+------+-------------+

    Parameters
    ----------
    ds : Dataset
        The :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset` containing the Image Pixel module
        and *Pixel Data*.
    unit : str, optional
        If ``'bytes'`` then returns the expected length of the *Pixel Data* in
        whole bytes and NOT including an odd length trailing NULL padding
        byte. If ``'pixels'`` then returns the expected length of the *Pixel
        Data* in terms of the total number of pixels (default ``'bytes'``).

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The expected length of the *Pixel Data* in either whole bytes or
        pixels, excluding the NULL trailing padding byte for odd length data.
    """
    rows = cast(int, ds.Rows)
    columns = cast(int, ds.Columns)
    samples_per_pixel = cast(int, ds.SamplesPerPixel)
    bits_allocated = cast(int, ds.BitsAllocated)

    length = rows * columns * samples_per_pixel
    length *= get_nr_frames(ds)

    if unit == "pixels":
        return length

    # Correct for the number of bytes per pixel
    if bits_allocated == 1:
        # Determine the nearest whole number of bytes needed to contain
        #   1-bit pixel data. e.g. 10 x 10 1-bit pixels is 100 bits, which
        #   are packed into 12.5 -> 13 bytes
        length = length // 8 + (length % 8 > 0)
    else:
        length *= bits_allocated // 8

    # DICOM Standard, Part 4, Annex C.7.6.3.1.2

        length = length // 3 * 2

    return length
